headline: COPPER SMASHES ALL-TIME RECORD at $6.60/lb; Sulfuric Acid Crunch Threatens 20% of Global Mine Supply
snippet: Copper futures hit a fresh all-time record of $6.60/lb ($14,550/tonne) on Wednesday as robust Chinese smelter activity collides with a supply shock — the US-Iran conflict has all but suspended Middle Eastern sulfur exports since March, and roughly one-fifth of global copper production relies on sulfuric acid derived from that sulfur.

headline: GOLD RETREATS TO $4,678: CPI Hits 3.8%, Strait of Hormuz Shutdown Keeps Rate-Cut Hopes Buried
snippet: Gold fell to $4,678/oz on Tuesday — down 16% from its $5,589 January peak — as US CPI surprised at 3.8%, the highest reading since May 2023, while the prolonged Strait of Hormuz shutdown keeps oil elevated and rate-cut expectations priced out through year-end.

headline: BARRICK BEATS Q1 GUIDANCE: 719K oz Gold, EPS Surges 256%, $1,708 AISC Against $4,861 Realized Price
snippet: Barrick Mining's Q1 2026 earnings showed a 256% year-over-year EPS jump to $0.96/share as the company produced 719,000 oz — well above its 640K–680K guidance range — at a $1,708 AISC against a $4,861 realized gold price, sustaining its full-year target of 2.9–3.25 million ounces.

headline: OceanaGold HITS 30.64 g/t Gold over 15.5m at Haile; Multiple High-Grade Underground Zones Confirmed
snippet: OceanaGold's Horseshoe Underground at the Haile Gold Mine in South Carolina returned 15.5m @ 30.64 g/t Au and 30.5m @ 13.86 g/t Au, confirming a high-grade orebody expanding at depth and supporting a potential underground transition beneath the existing open pit.

headline: BRUNSWICK DRILLS 123m AT 0.72% Li2O in James Bay; High-Grade Cesium Also Emerges at Anatacau Main
snippet: Brunswick Exploration (TSXV: BRW) intersected 17.7m @ 1.10% Li2O within a 123m @ 0.72% Li2O package at Anatacau Main in Quebec's James Bay, with the mineralized corridor now drill-traced over 500m — and three more drill holes with results pending, including one that hit additional pegmatites.

headline: CAMECO HALTS Key Lake Uranium Mill After Bridge Collapse; McArthur River Output Cut, 1.5M lbs at Risk
snippet: Cameco has shut down its Key Lake mill and reduced output at McArthur River — one of the world's largest uranium mines — after northern Saskatchewan flooding collapsed the Smoothstone River Bridge, severing the primary supply route for critical operating materials. Direct production impact is estimated at 1.5 million lbs with no confirmed timeline for resumption.

headline: SILVER HITS $84.53 as China Imports 790+ Tons YTD; Sixth Straight Annual Supply Deficit Forecast
snippet: Silver crossed $84.53/oz on Tuesday — up more than $51 from a year ago and 150% higher over two years — with the Silver Institute projecting a sixth consecutive annual supply deficit of roughly 67 million oz in 2026, driven by Chinese solar demand that absorbed 790+ tonnes in the first months of the year alone.

headline: Chile Lithium Carbonate Exports SURGE 175% to $498M in April as SQM-Codelco JV Ramps Production
snippet: Chile's April 2026 mining exports hit $5.96 billion (+14.1%), with lithium carbonate revenues surging 175.6% year-over-year to $498 million as the SQM-Codelco joint venture ramps production — a direct marker of how supply is finally chasing the energy storage and EV demand wave.

headline: Gold Stock Weakness Creating M&A OPENINGS as Producer Cash Flow Hits Records — Feneck | Kitco
snippet: Analyst John Feneck argues that gold equities trading at compressed multiples despite record operating margins at $4,700+ gold is historically the setup that precedes either institutional re-rating or M&A activity — with junior and mid-tier producers not yet seeing the institutional bid as the most likely targets.

headline: GOLD $5,000 STILL IN PLAY: Why Institutional Forecasters Haven't Abandoned the Bull Case
snippet: Despite gold's 16% pullback from its $5,589 January peak, major banks including J.P. Morgan and Goldman Sachs maintain year-end targets above current levels, citing structural central bank demand, persistent dollar weakness, and Middle East risk premiums that show no sign of unwinding.

headline: RARE EARTH NdPr SHEDS 21% IN APRIL Despite 88% Year-to-Date Gain; Correction or Reversal?
snippet: NdPr oxide fell 21% in April 2026 to $99.61/kg — its sharpest monthly decline since the Q1 rally began — though the metal still sits 88% above its January open, leaving Western producers like MP Materials and Lynas well above their operational cost bases while the market debates whether this is a pause or a peak.
